The '''2006 World Championship''' was the 11th Star Wars CCG World Championship, run by the [[Players Committee]] on 19–22 October 2006 at PasTimes, a game store in Niles, Illinois, near Chicago.<ref name="f12542">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=12542 Day 3 Results], mc9457, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, "[FY06] Worlds Weekend 2006" (23 October 2006). The forum header reads "October 19th - October 22nd / PasTimes; 8351 1/2 Golf Road; Niles, Illinois 60714".</ref><ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org; Wayback [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ 17 August 2023]</ref> It had been planned for August 2006; in June the Players Committee reported that PasTimes was working with it on a new date because the August date conflicted with other events.<ref name="pc-jun06">[http://www.swccgpc.com/ SWCCGPC.com] (home page; news item "World's Date Change - Your Vote Matters", admin_mike, 16 June 2006: "PasTimes in Chicago is working with us in order to provide a new date. August date conflicted with other pre-planned events."). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060617215932/http://www.swccgpc.com/ Internet Archive]</ref> Earlier, on 27 April 2006, the Committee had announced that "a pretty major announcement in regards to Worlds" had been made on its message boards, in a news item titled "Worlds and Nationals Discussion".<ref name="pc-news2006">[http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&new_topic News], swccgpc.com (27 April 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060617220030/http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&new_topic Internet Archive]</ref> Wikipedia gives a field of 34.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia (World Championship table)</ref> [[Nate Meeker]] topped the twelve-player Day 3 standings on differential and then beat [[Brian Hunter]] in a two-game final, losing game 1 by 1 and winning game 2 by 3.<ref name="f12542" /><ref name="awards" /> Meeker posted his Day 3 Dark deck, "Scum Solid", on DeckTech, but that list was not archived and is not on the wiki.<ref name="f12556">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=12556 Players at Worlds (Post all decklist links here)], Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums (24 October – November 2006)</ref>

The constructed pool was printed Decipher cards through [[Theed Palace]] plus the original [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)|Players Committee Virtual Sets]] then legal: [[Premiere - Original VS6]], since Virtual Sets 7–11 became legal only on 4 December 2006 (see [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]]).

== Planning ==

On 4 April 2006 [[Michael Carr|Mike Carr]], a Players Committee Advocate, announced that the 2006 Nationals would be held at GenCon and Worlds at PasTimes in Chicago "the last weekend in August".<ref name="pcf-9457-130851">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=130851#130851 Road to Worlds 2006], Mike Carr (mc9457), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (4 April 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060617221844/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=131173 Internet Archive]</ref> Two days later he gave the expected dates as 24–27 August 2006, and [[Brandon Schele]] gave the store's address as 8351 Golf Road, Niles, Illinois.<ref name="pcf-9457-131145">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=131145#131145 Road to Worlds 2006], Mike Carr (mc9457), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (6 April 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060617221844/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=131173 Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-9457-131166">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=131166#131166 Road to Worlds 2006], Brandon Schele (The Jedi Knight), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (6 April 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060617221844/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=131173 Internet Archive]</ref>

On 6 May 2006 Carr explained why Worlds was leaving GenCon. GenCon charged the Committee $1.50 an hour for each player in its gaming area, and each player also needed a $65–$75 pass; since 2005 GenCon had charged separately for each day of a multi-day event. To make up the roughly $2,500 in cash given away in 2005, Day 1, Day 2 and the cash consolation tournament would each have cost about $37 to enter. Origins had been the Committee's first choice, but "our experience with them turned sour this year". A hotel near GenCon on the same weekend was also ruled out, because the area's hotels had contracted with GenCon not to open their convention rooms that weekend without GenCon's permission. Chicago, New York, Los Angeles and Las Vegas were considered as central locations; New York was ruled out on cost, and Los Angeles and Las Vegas for lack of volunteers close by and of stores open to hosting events. PasTimes was chosen for its low cost, ample playing space and good history with Star Wars CCG, and Comic Images was about to hold its own world championship there. The dates were picked to avoid Origins, GenCon and DragonCon without starting so late that college players would miss it. [[Kevin Brownell]] was the Committee's contact with PasTimes; Carr wrote that he had forgotten to tell Brownell to request the date, so it had never been fully confirmed with the store.<ref name="pcf-9457-135624">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=135624#135624 Road to Worlds 2006], Mike Carr (mc9457), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (6 May 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618072946/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=138185&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref> The same day Carr said the weekend would have a price structure covering Worlds, sealed events, an InstanTournament Championship and a [[Young Jedi]] Championship, and that there might be a single "badge fee" for all of it.<ref name="pcf-9457-135630">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=135630#135630 Road to Worlds 2006], Mike Carr (mc9457), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (6 May 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618072946/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=138185&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref>

On 25 May 2006 Carr reported that PasTimes had said nothing was guaranteed yet but saw no problems with the dates,<ref name="pcf-9457-138558">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=138558#138558 Road to Worlds 2006], Mike Carr (mc9457), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 May 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618072946/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=138185&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref> and on 31 May that PasTimes was rescheduling a PTQ it had planned for that weekend.<ref name="pcf-9457-139109">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=139109#139109 Road to Worlds 2006], Mike Carr (mc9457), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (31 May 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618001452/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=139704 Internet Archive]</ref> On 15 June 2006 Carr announced that the date would change, because the current date structure did not work for PasTimes, which was working with the Committee on alternatives.<ref name="pcf-9457-141299">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=141299#141299 Road to Worlds 2006], Mike Carr (mc9457), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060617221315/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=9457&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=120 Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-10323-141302">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=141302#141302 Worlds Date], Mike Carr (mc9457), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618073156/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=10323&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref> Players were asked to vote on a new date;<ref name="pc-jun06" /> PasTimes had no open September dates other than Labor Day weekend.<ref name="pcf-10323-141409">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=141409#141409 Worlds Date], Mike Carr (mc9457), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618073156/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=10323&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref> Carr wrote that GenCon was "not an option" and that PasTimes was discussing hotel possibilities with the Committee,<ref name="pcf-10323-141343">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=141343#141343 Worlds Date], Mike Carr (mc9457), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618073156/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=10323&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref> and [[Nick Kolnik]] wrote that moving Worlds away from GenCon was not about "saving money" but about the Committee "NOT GOING BROKE".<ref name="pcf-10323-141337">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=141337#141337 Worlds Date], Nick Kolnik (bluethrawn), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618073156/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=10323&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref>

On 12 July 2006 Carr announced a confirmed date: Friday to Sunday, 20–22 October 2006, Days 1–3, again at PasTimes in Chicago.<ref name="sf-10759-147185">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=147185#p147185 CONFIRMED:  Worlds Date], Michael Carr (mc9457), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (12 July 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20210127075535/https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=10759 Internet Archive]</ref> On 2 August [[Kevin Brownell]] wrote that Day 3 would also have the third annual Worlds Consolation Tournament, with virtual card design and cash prizes, which he called his own contribution to the Worlds scene.<ref name="sf-10759-153847">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=153847#p153847 CONFIRMED:  Worlds Date], Kevin Brownell (CubsFan), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (2 August 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261125170730/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t10759-start60.html Internet Archive]</ref> Carr's tentative schedule of 6 August 2006 moved the event to Thursday–Saturday: Day 1 on Thursday, Day 2 on Friday and Day 3 on Saturday, each starting at 1 pm with registration from 11 am and deck checks from noon, and the finals at about 8 pm. The Worlds Consolation Cash Tournament was to start on Saturday at 3 pm, a V-lite tournament was planned for a date to be decided, and constructed instant tournaments ([[Open]], [[Classic]], [[No Such Thing As Luck]]) and sealed ones ([[Official Tournament Sealed Deck|OTSD]], [[Secret Squirrel]]) were to run through the weekend, along with a chance to talk to the advocates.<ref name="sf-10759-155119">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=155119#p155119 CONFIRMED:  Worlds Date], Michael Carr (mc9457), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (6 August 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261125170730/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t10759-start60.html Internet Archive]</ref> The next day Carr explained that the 20–22 October dates had been given early in the discussion; when the plans were discussed with PasTimes, the Sunday times could be accommodated by neither the Advocates nor the store, so the dates were changed.<ref name="sf-10759-155300">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=155300#p155300 CONFIRMED:  Worlds Date], Michael Carr (mc9457), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (7 August 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261125170810/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t10759-start80.html Internet Archive]</ref> On 24 August a volunteer posting as NateA apologised that, told on 14 August to post the change of dates, he had updated the calendar but not the main page of the website.<ref name="sf-10759-160692">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=160692#p160692 CONFIRMED:  Worlds Date], NateA, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (24 August 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261125170523/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t10759-start140.html Internet Archive]</ref> On 25 August Carr locked the thread and said a new topic would give the new date.<ref name="sf-10759-160732">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=160732#p160732 CONFIRMED:  Worlds Date], Michael Carr (mc9457), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (25 August 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261125170523/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t10759-start140.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Top 8 bracket ===

There was no elimination bracket: Day 3 was played as standings among twelve players, and the top two met in a two-game final.<ref name="f12542" /> Individual Day 3 game results were not published.

* Final, game 1: Brian Hunter (Dark) beat Nate Meeker (Light) by 1
* Final, game 2: Nate Meeker (Dark) beat Brian Hunter (Light) by 3

The Players Committee announced Meeker as the 2006 World Champion.<ref name="f12542" />
